subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Algeria 2030 (National Digital Transformation Strategy)
position_end: Targets unchanged: all public services online by 2030, 500,000 ICT jobs
note: targets 100% of public services online by 2030, 500,000 ICT jobs and 20% of GDP from the digital economy

subject: gov.policy
name: Digitalisation oversight and the national portal
milestone: Sole official address of the national portal confirmed, July 2026
position_start: The high commission for digitalisation created by presidential decree of 6 September 2023, and the national digital development agency by decree of 26 November 2019, whose article 5 requires the national digital strategy to be prepared
position_end: The high commission confirmed a single official address for the national portal in July 2026 after impersonating sites appeared, and a Council of Ministers sitting in June 2026 took presentations on digitalisation. The strategy the 2019 decree requires is the 2025-2030 national digital transformation strategy on five axes and 25 objectives, separately held

subject: gov.policy
name: High Commission for Digitalisation (Decree 23-314) and its scientific committee
position_end: 15-member scientific and technical committee seated, three from the diaspora
note: High Commissioner Meriem Benmouloud; a 15-member scientific and technical committee, three of them from the diaspora, launched 2025-10-23

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to information under the media organic law
position_end: The organic law governing media and information activity includes provisions requiring public bodies to facilitate journalists' access to information; there is no general right-to-information statute on the base, and no request, refusal or appeal under these provisions is recorded

subject: gov.legislate
name: Domestic online-platform regulation (local presence, takedown, data residency)
position_end: Under examination; bill text not held and adoption not established
note: proposition de loi deposited by deputy Bouhali Abdelbasset, reported under examination at the APN; would bind platforms above one million users in Algeria to a local office, a legal representative, in-country data storage, takedown within 24 hours and six-monthly compliance reports, and would create a regulator attached to the Presidency; provisions are the outlet’s reading, the bill text is not held, and nothing on file establishes adoption (2026-08-04)

subject: gov.legislate
name: General authorisation regime for cloud services
position_end: A regulator decision implementing an executive decree and fixing the licensing procedure for cloud services - a regulatory instrument rather than a strategy, and the only cloud-specific rule the base holds

subject: gov.legislate
name: Law 18-05 on electronic commerce
position_end: In force; the great majority of online selling runs through social-media pages outside its obligations, with cash on delivery dominant (2026-08)
note: the assessment is named-analyst opinion from the Organisation nationale d'orientation et de protection du consommateur dans le commerce electronique, not a state position; the law's own date and text are not held, and no enforcement action or compliance figure is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Law 26-02 on trust services and electronic identification
position_end: The national trust-service and electronic-identification framework, running to 116 articles; its article 27 requires trust-service-provider data to be hosted nationally. It makes no mention of artificial intelligence

subject: gov.legislate
name: National data governance system
milestone: Launched by the prime minister, 9 February 2026
position_end: The prime minister launched the national data-governance system established by a presidential decree of 30 December 2025 at a ceremony in the capital; the decree's own text is separately on this ledger and no operating rule, dataset or participating body under the system is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: National information-verification ("fact-checking") system
milestone: Draft before the Council of Government 2026-07-23
position_end: Draft examined; no regulator, legal basis or oversight mechanism named
note: draft examined by the Council of Government; no regulator, legal basis or oversight mechanism is named in anything held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Payment service provider regime
milestone: Anti-money-laundering regulation extended to payment providers, 24 September 2025
position_start: The first regulatory instrument dedicated to payment service providers, adopted by the central bank on 14 April 2025
position_end: A second regulation of September 2025 explicitly brings payment service providers inside the anti-money-laundering regime. Both sit under the monetary and banking law of June 2023, which repealed the prior ordinance, and the banking commission issued guidelines on virtual assets in November 2025

subject: gov.legislate
name: Presidential Decree 25-320 — national public-data governance framework
position_end: 20 articles in force; art. 19 classification and cataloguing not shown to have commenced

note: 20 articles in JO n.87; art. 15 gives the data-protection authority a supervisory hook and art. 18 excludes defence, security and judicial data; its art. 19 classification and cataloguing duties are not shown to have commenced The system the decree establishes was launched by the prime minister at a ceremony on 9 February 2026, which this ledger holds separately.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics law and the statistics office
milestone: Oversight of the statistics office transferred by presidential decree, 10 November 2025
position_start: The 1994 legislative decree as the governing statistics law, with the office's organisation set by a 1995 decree whose article 6 makes it responsible for the technical preparation, conduct, processing and analysis of population censuses
position_end: A presidential decree of 10 November 2025 transferred oversight of the statistics office, and a Council of Ministers sitting the same autumn took its modernisation. The office's own presentation to an international quality workshop in July 2025 names the 1994 legislative decree as the governing law, so the statute is thirty-two years old while the institution around it is being rearranged

subject: gov.protect
name: ANPDP deliberation treating images as personal data
position_end: Images treated as personal data; deliberation no. 04, effective on publication on the Authority's own website, no Journal officiel step; full text now held
note: deliberation no. 04 of 15 July 2026, adopted by the Authority's members in sitting under Loi n. 18-07 as amended; article 06 holds that publishing images via platforms hosted, storing or processing data, or reachable, from outside Algeria is a transfer of data outside national territory under arts. 44-45; article 11 provides the deliberation takes effect on publication on the Authority's own website, with no Journal officiel step; twelve members are named; full text is now held

subject: gov.regional

position_end: The country's ratification of the regional information and communication technologies organisation's founding agreement; no activity, obligation or harmonisation instrument under it appears on the base

subject: gov.regional
name: Arab Maghreb Union treaty
position_end: In force since 1 July 1989 with a binding judicial organ, and no summit held since 1994 - a legal frame for regional harmonisation with no active machinery behind it

subject: gov.regional

position_start: The 2018 law's chapter IV, notably article 44, setting a prior-authorisation and adequacy regime for transfers abroad
position_end: The regime was carried into the amending law of July 2025. The authority's own compliance guide describes an operational portal and states that processing involving transfer requires its authorisation; no adequacy decision or authorisation count is published

subject: gov.regional

position_end: The ministry's programme targets 7 million connected households by the end of 2027, and the country's statement to the international development conference restated its fibre and fifth-generation connectivity targets alongside a trans-Saharan backbone corridor
